Resolves #18682

🌿 A spec that wanted two windows apart used to copy someone's numbers and inherit their guesses; the copy that looked careful measured its fit against a screen the emulator invented, so it could refuse a stage that existed and accept one that did not — after this there is nowhere left to keep a private opinion about where a window goes.

**What this delivers.** The adoption half of #18682, on top of the extraction that merged as #18689. Three spec files stop carrying their own native-window placement: 244 lines of duplication leave them, 157 arrive in the module that already owned the job, and `placePopupOutsideSource` — the name this ticket was filed around — is now zero across the tree.

**The defect this ticket is named for was hiding in the copy I had called the careful one.** `DemoBCrossWindowDragNL` polled real `outerWidth`/`screenX`, fell back through four candidate slots measured against `screen.avail*`, and threw when none fitted. It looked like the rigorous implementation. But both Demo B specs run at an emulated 760×720 with `screen` faked to 1920×1080, so that fit test — and its throw — were evaluated against a stage that does not exist. It had the blind copy's defect wearing a fit test, which is worse than the blind copy, because it reports confidence.

**So the module refuses to guess.** `placeBesideSource` trusts an envelope only when the caller declares one or the page is unemulated. Otherwise it skips the pre-check rather than run it against fiction, places beside the source, and then proves the arrangement by measuring it — `expect.poll` on real non-overlap is the receipt either way. A fit test that cannot be trusted is replaced by an observation that can, and the verdict carries `stageTrusted` so a caller can tell which one it got.

**The product gets first refusal.** Headed browsers honour the app's own placement once the popup connects, so the helper polls the observable rects first and moves nothing when the two windows already miss each other. Only a genuinely overlapping stage reaches CDP. That is why the verdict has a `moved: false` case: the cheapest correct answer to a placement request is often to leave the windows where the product put them.

Evidence: L3 (e2e tier on this host, re-measured at the corrected head — the three touched specs run with real popup windows placed through CDP and their rects measured) → L3 required (AC-5 is a preservation bound; only a real run can measure whether an arm stayed red for its own reason). Residual: AC-6, Residual-Owner: #18532.

The consolidation restores the chrome-inset stability assertion, both app-root assertions, the receipt log and every assertion message the local copy had shed |
| AC-2 | Delivered by #18689, verified live here: `WorkstationFiveBeatNL:13` imports `planSideBySide` and `readDisplayEnvelope`, consumes them at `:1970-1975` as `plan = planSideBySide(screen)` with `expect(plan.fits, plan.reason ?? …)`, and retains no inline copy — `screen.avail*` is absent from the file |

| AC-4 | The fit test reads a stage it can trust or none, and the authority is decided BEFORE any verdict including the no-move one (`095e8504eb`, @neo-gpt-emmy R1 RA-1). Containment is three-valued so "cannot be established" never reads as "yes"; the docblock states what a `fits` verdict promises — non-overlap always, display containment only when `stageTrusted`. **The prescribed spec change is superseded rather than done** — see Evolution |

| AC-7 | Resolved on the ticket as a recorded bound, not a built capability: a pin cannot be computed honestly under emulation, it could not have fixed the arms it was raised for, and no caller is left |

## Deltas from ticket

`rectsOverlap` is exported rather than kept private. It is the question a caller asks *before* deciding to move anything, and the helper's own "are they already apart" poll is the first consumer; leaving it unexported would have forced the next spec to re-derive an interval test that is easy to get subtly wrong at the touching edge.

One scope addition beyond the ticket: the JSDoc repair in `cd6ace96df`. It is not an AC, it is a gap I found reading my own diff before handing it over — the ticket points the next reader at an option that was undocumented.

## Test Evidence

All three touched specs are Brain-gated, so CI does not run them. Run on this host with `NEO_AGENTOS_RUNTIME_ROOT` set, `-c test/playwright/playwright.config.e2e.mjs --workers=1`:

| Spec | Result | Recorded at base |
|---|---|---|
| `DemoBCrossWindowDragNL` | 3 red at `:248` / `:453` / `:695` | same three lines |
| `DemoBPerspectivesNL` | 1 red at `:144` | same line |
| `WorkstationTearOutSourceContinuityNL` | 1 red at `:596`, 2 passed | same line, same 1/2 split |

The reasons are the product's, not the rig's: "the real gesture must settle through the remote target", "the product must publish strict park admission", "the real popup hosts the live workbench pane", and the `#16756` stage wanting a 1200px-wide native display headless cannot provide. **No placement assertion appears among any failure** — `the staged windows must end up physically non-overlapping` never fires.

The same run proves the helper positively. `DemoBCrossWindowDragNL`'s diagnostic reports the source at `left: 22, width: 760` and the target at `left: 822, width: 600` — `22 + 760 + 40` to the pixel, non-overlapping, placed through the untrusted-envelope path on a page whose `screen` is faked. The arrangement the module claims is the arrangement the windows took.

`test/playwright/unit/e2e/filmStage.spec.mjs`: 19/19, including a planned target never overlapping the source it was planned beside, the fallback order right → left → below → above, and three arms for the no-move verdict at @neo-gpt-emmy R1 numbers — two of which are red at the parent commit and the 1600-wide control which must stay green on both sides.

## Post-Merge Validation

- [ ] `WorkstationFiveBeatNL`'s film path stays gated behind `NEO_FILM_TAKE=1` and `darwin`; the first capture night on this branch is where the staged take is observed, and that belongs to whoever runs it
- [ ] #18532's re-show witness gets written on top of `placeBesideSource`, which is AC-6 and this PR's one declared residual

## Commits
- `91a93345e9` — a target can be planned beside an already-placed source
- `c3a2a4e634` — a stage is planned only against an envelope worth trusting
- `1221d6bd52` — the last two placement copies collapse into the shared helper
- `28c3a27fbb` — the continuity spec consumes the shared stage helpers it was duplicating
- `cd6ace96df` — the option AC-7b sends the next caller to is documented where they land
- `095e8504eb` — a no-move verdict answers only for a stage it actually checked (R1 RA-1 + RA-2)

## Evolution

AC-4 asked that specs placing real windows declare `viewport: null` per-test, following `DemoBVesselConversionNL:133`. I did not do that, and the reason is worth the paragraph. `DemoBCrossWindowDragNL:133-135` documents its emulated viewport as load-bearing: both physical viewports must fit side by side because global screen-space hit-testing deliberately resolves the first intersecting window. Converting that spec to `viewport: null` would change the stage its drag rows depend on to fix a fit test — repairing the instrument by breaking the experiment. So the module absorbs the problem instead: it declines to trust an envelope it knows is fictional, and proves the arrangement by measurement. What AC-4 now guarantees, stated as the bound rather than as an intent met: **non-overlap always, measured on the real rects** — and **display containment unproven whenever no trustworthy envelope exists**, which is precisely the emulated case these two specs are in. `stageTrusted` is how a caller tells the two apart, and a caller that needs containment declares an `envelope`. So the prescribed mechanism is superseded and the guarantee is narrower than the original wording implied; `viewport: null` remains the right answer for any spec that does not need the emulation. #18682's AC-4 row and its ledger comment carry the same text.
